spacr._gpu_governor:
Keep spaCR's GPU work inside the memory a shared card has free.

A workstation GPU is often shared by several jobs: a segmentation run, a
measurement run and a training run can all hold memory on one card. Each of
them sizes its batches for an empty card, so whichever allocates last runs
out of memory and, before this module, stopped. This module is the one place
that decides how much a spaCR GPU call may take:

* before each batch it reads the free memory of the device and, when the
  batch is estimated not to fit with ``gpu_memory_margin_gb`` to spare,
  shrinks the batch or waits for memory to be freed;
* on an out-of-memory error from PyTorch or CuPy it releases the cached
  blocks, halves the batch and retries the same item; after a few failed
  retries at batch size 1 the item runs on the CPU. No item is dropped and
  the run never stops on an out-of-memory error;
* after each item it releases the cached memory, so a co-tenant can use it;
* after a run of clean items it doubles the batch again, up to the size the
  caller asked for;
* ``gpu_memory_fraction`` sets a hard ceiling through
  ``torch.cuda.set_per_process_memory_fraction``. That call caps the memory
  PyTorch's caching allocator RESERVES, which is more than it has allocated
  by the allocator's fragmentation, so every need and cap here is sized from
  ``torch.cuda.max_memory_reserved`` and never below 1.5 times the allocated
  peak; a ceiling set lower than what the work needs is raised, with a
  message, rather than turning every larger item into an out-of-memory retry;
* when CUDA has not been initialised yet and ``PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF`` is
  unset, :func:`_configure` sets it to ``expandable_segments:True``, which
  lets the allocator grow segments in place instead of reserving new ones,
  so reserved memory stays close to allocated memory. An existing value is
  never changed, and a process that already holds a CUDA context keeps the
  allocator it has;
* every process is counted with about 0.4 GB of CUDA context on top of what
  its allocator reserves, in the ledger and in the budget;
* a ledger file under the user cache directory records what every spaCR GPU
  process on the machine is using and about to claim, so a new job counts
  what the others are about to take and a running job shrinks while room is
  needed. Entries of processes that no longer exist are ignored;
* while a site is adapting, a line such as ``[gpu] site=measure_intensity
  items=200 shrinks=0 oom_retries=6 cpu_fallbacks=2 (1.0%)`` is printed
  every 50 items or 60 seconds, and a warning when more than 3 % of a site's
  items ran on the CPU;
* every item's compute path (``gpu`` or ``cpu``) is recorded. Measure writes
  it as a ``compute_path`` column on its object rows when ``measure_gpu`` is
  on, and the run report says whether the run stayed on one path.
  ``gpu_fallback_policy='pause'`` never falls back: an item that does not
  fit even at batch size 1 waits for the GPU instead, so a run stays on one
  path;
* the shrink, wait, retry, fallback and ramp-up counts are summarised in the
  run log at the end of a run.

``gpu_adaptive_batch=False`` turns the batch control off: every call then
runs exactly as asked, with only the optional fraction applied. On a machine
without a visible CUDA device every call also runs exactly as asked.

spacr.illumination.IlluminationField.cor:
Correct a crop window cut from a field, without the rest of the field.

The gain and offset maps are sliced to the window's place in the
field, so every pixel gets exactly the value the whole-field
correction gives it: ``(observed - dark) * (1 / flatfield)`` in
float32.

:param window: ``(h, w, C)`` intensities, or ``(h, w)`` for one
    channel, cut from a field of this plate at rows ``y0:y0 + h`` and
    columns ``x0:x0 + w``.
:param channels: the merged-stack channel of each plane of
    ``window``, in order.
:param y0: the field row of the window's first row. It may be
    negative, as for a window zero-padded past the field's edge
    (:meth:`spacr.crops.MergedField.read_window`).
:param x0: the field column of the window's first column; negative
    allowed as for ``y0``.
:returns: the corrected window as float32, in ``window``'s shape.
    Pixels that lie outside the field are padding and come back as
    0.
:raises IlluminationError: when the window has no pixel inside the
    field, its channel count differs from ``channels``, or the model
    does not cover one of the channels.
